gpus.name: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090

nvlink.note: Two cards only, with the GeForce RTX NVLink bridge (3-way/4-way not supported). The GA102 whitepaper gives 112.5 GB/s total between two GPUs for the GA102 NVLink interface (four x4 links, 14.0625 GB/s per link per direction) and says two RTX 3090 GPUs can be connected using NVLink; it does not repeat the figure per product.

gpus.p2pNote: GeForce: no NVIDIA statement found for PCIe peer-to-peer on the RTX 3090 (NVIDIA staff said "Peer to Peer is not supported on 4090" and that RTX 50-series GeForce do not support it, but nothing NVIDIA-official names the 3090). Users report P2P working over the NVLink bridge only. Treat as not available over PCIe unless the driver reports it (simpleP2P / nvidia-smi topo -p2p r).

gpus.notes: Per GPU of HGX B300 (8 Blackwell Ultra GPUs). NVIDIA's current documents state 270 GB HBM3e per HGX B300 GPU (HGX/DGX B300 totals 2.1 TB), not 288 GB: 288 GB is the Blackwell Ultra chip maximum (blog: 'Available SM count and HBM capacity varies by SKU'). nvidia-smi reports 275040 MiB = 268.6 GiB = 288.4 GB decimal. Blackwell Ultra vs B200: FP4 dense 14 vs 9 PF (1.5x), 2x attention-layer acceleration (SFU EX2 10.7 vs 5 TExp/s per the blog), FP64 cut to 1.2 TFLOPS (B200: 37) and INT8 cut to 0.15/0.30 POPS dense/sparse (B200: 4.5/9). INT8: the datasheet's sparse figure is 307 TOPS, the technical brief's 0.30 POPS; the brief's dense/sparse pair is used. Memory bandwidth 7.7 TB/s per GPU (HGX B300 total 62 TB/s).
